item.title: Scientists discover silk traces on 101 ancient objects in China, uncover clues to ancient rituals
item.description: Scientists studying 3,000-year-old objects from China's Sanxingdui archaeological site have found silk traces on 101 artefacts, including bronze masks, gold, jade and ivory objects. Published in the journal Antiquity, the study suggests that ancient Shu people used silk to wrap or cover objects during rituals. Researchers also identified red pigments and different weaving patterns, offering clues about ancient textile practices.

item.title: Australia’s stingless bees may help fight antibiotic resistance
item.description: Researchers at the University of Sydney are investigating the medicinal properties of honey from stingless bees. The honey has shown effectiveness against various bacterial and fungal pathogens, including difficult-to-treat strains. Findings suggest that sugarbag honey is comparable in strength to well-known medical-grade honeys. While propolis displayed selective antimicrobial activity, the reason for honey's potency remains unclear. Further research is needed to identify the beneficial compounds within the honey.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Arkansas couple pays $8,000 for access to landlocked property, loses court battle with neighbours
item.description: An Arkansas couple who paid their neighbours $8,000 for an 18-foot-wide road to access their land near Beaver Lake have lost a dispute over its location. The Arkansas Court of Appeals upheld a route along the neighbours' property boundary, despite concerns about construction costs and difficult terrain. One judge disagreed, warning that the approved route could be unusable without expensive work.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: German teacher on sick leave for 16 years, collected nearly €1 million in salary; now faces fraud charges over €248,000
item.description: A 62-year-old German educator faces fraud charges after reportedly taking a 16-year sick leave, during which she allegedly collected over €248,000 in salary. Investigators believe she fabricated medical documentation to support her prolonged absence from the classroom. Although she engaged in scuba diving, there’s no evidence of her undertaking any other professional work. The court is currently reviewing the case to determine if a full trial is warranted.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Israel election results: Neither Netanyahu nor oppn wins majority; what happens next?
item.description: Israel faces a political deadlock after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc fell short of the 61 seats needed for a majority. With Arab-led parties holding 19 seats, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot could seek their support to form a government. However, ideological differences complicate the numbers. A unity government, opposition defections or another election are among four possible scenarios, according to CNN.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: University of Georgia secures $8 million NOAA grant to plan restoration of acres of salt marsh
item.description: University of Georgia has received an $8 million grant to restore salt marsh habitat across four coastal states. The initiative, which spans from North Carolina to Florida, will assess the use of dredged sediment. This project aims to elevate marshes and support diverse wildlife while addressing rising sea levels and pollution. Proposed restoration sites include Bird-Long Island, Cape Lookout National Seashore, Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge, and Julia’s Island.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: An Ohio appeals court on Oct 26 upheld a zoning ban on Airbnb rentals in a 140-home neighbourhood
item.description: An Ohio appellate court has confirmed a zoning restriction prohibiting short-term rentals in a suburban area. Michael A. Clevenger, an owner looking to operate an Airbnb, faced opposition from neighbors concerned about excessive noise, parking congestion, and heightened safety risks from frequent guests. This ruling emphasizes the importance of adhering to local zoning regulations that maintain the integrity of residential neighborhoods, reinforcing existing legal frameworks against short-term rental operations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A $295 million Malibu mansion by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Tadao Ando was quietly on the market when Kanye West came unannounced
item.description: Kanye West made an unplanned visit to a stunning Malibu mansion crafted by Tadao Ando, spending four days there. He secured a stay without prior arrangement, likening his presence to that of Elvis Presley. Meanwhile, the estate was later sold to Jay-Z and Beyoncé, breaking sales records. West's personal Ando-designed property, however, is grappling with legal and financial troubles, leaving its future uncertain due to ongoing foreclosure issues.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Maine Forest Protections Secure Jobs: Coalition preserves 27,000 acres; working forest still supports timber, recreation
item.description: In a remarkable achievement, over 27,000 acres of forestland in western Maine have been safeguarded through collaborative conservation efforts. This extensive initiative spanned six years, bringing together environmental groups, state agencies, and local trusts. Preserving this land is vital for ensuring clean drinking water for more than 200,000 residents while supporting timber jobs and enhancing recreational opportunities and habitats for wildlife in the area.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Once a textile giant, now homes and offices: Virginia’s abandoned mill gets a $110 million makeover
item.description: Dan River Falls embodies a transformative redevelopment of the historic White Mill, originally constructed in 1920, located in Danville. Completed in November 2024, the first phase features 190 residential apartments. Plans for the future include developing a vibrant riverfront park and retail area. This public-private collaboration strives to maintain the mill's historic integrity while breathing new life into the community and catering to workforce housing needs.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Cleopatra’s eye makeup secret? Ancient Egyptians used lead-based kohl
item.description: In ancient Egypt, kohl was more than just a cosmetic; it served dual purposes, enhancing beauty while protecting the eyes. Studies indicate that its ingredients could boost immune responses, making it a valuable tool for health. Both men and women embraced the use of black and green powders, and ancient texts highlight the fusion of cosmetics with medicine, revealing the intricate beliefs surrounding beauty and wellness in that era.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Taylor Swift gave $100,000 to a flood-hit Tennessee playground; now $3 million grant is sought
item.description: In 2010, Taylor Swift made a significant contribution of $100,000 to help rebuild the Kids Kingdom playground in Hendersonville after it was severely damaged by flooding. Originally built in 1996, the playground had encountered numerous safety challenges. Currently, officials are looking into a $3 million grant aimed at enhancing recreational facilities, particularly focusing on developing an all-inclusive playground for children of varying abilities.

item.title: Common daily fiber supplement was found to significantly reduce knee pain and improve strength
item.description: A recent study from the University of Nottingham unveils exciting findings regarding inulin supplementation for knee osteoarthritis. Participants not only experienced a reduction in joint pain, but they also enhanced their grip strength and sensitivity to pain. This research underscores the intriguing link between gut health and joint management, suggesting that dietary strategies might positively affect physical capabilities beyond just the painful areas.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Normal blood pressure may not tell the whole story: Scientists discover a brain ‘switch’
item.description: Hypertension impacts approximately 1.4 billion adults across the globe, with numerous individuals unaware of their status. A recent study by the University of Virginia uncovers essential brain cells responsible for maintaining stable blood pressure. These cells contribute to consistent blood pressure levels during daily activities and may mitigate abrupt changes.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Court Orders Pipeline Review: Judge sends Summit CO2 route back to PSC; zoning and safety re‑examined
item.description: A North Dakota court ruling requires state regulators to reassess the Summit Carbon Solutions pipeline's approval process and local zoning ordinances. Emmons and Burleigh counties are challenging the state’s authority over pipeline routes, focusing on setback requirements. The Public Service Commission must now clarify its safety assessments and reconsider alternative routing options. Summit's broader carbon capture project faces multiple regulatory issues across several states, complicating its future.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
